title: Stream-aware hydrator: checkpointed Pydantic/dataclass merging and idempotent retry helpers
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: SDK consumers increasingly use streaming LLM responses but need first-class typed hydration that can be incrementally merged as chunks arrive. Current helpers either require buffering full responses (bad for latency/memory) or provide ad-hoc merge code which is error-prone when retries, backpressure, or partial failures happen. Goal: implement a stream-aware hydration layer for the Python SDK that can incrementally apply partial parse results into Pydantic models and dataclasses, support checkpoint tokens for idempotent retries, and expose ergonomic helper functions/docs for application developers.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a StreamHydrator API that accepts chunked/parsing events and produces a final typed instance without buffering the entire raw payload
Hydrator must support Pydantic BaseModel and Python dataclasses interchangeably (first-class adapters)
Expose a lightweight checkpoint token feature that serializes minimal state so retries can resume without duplicating side-effects
Include examples demonstrating streaming of nested lists/maps where individual elements arrive across multiple chunks
Unit tests covering chunk reorder, duplicate-chunk idempotence, and recovery from transient parser errors
Integration example in examples/streaming_hydration_demo.py that runs against the hosted API streaming endpoint
technical_notes: Design choices: 1) Use an event-driven incremental parser that emits field-level updates (path + partial value) rather than re-parsing whole JSON on each chunk. 2) Hydration layer applies updates to a lightweight mutable representation and builds final Pydantic/dataclass instance only when 'finalized' marker is received. 3) Checkpoint token is a compact base64 of a monotonic chunk index + minimal changed-paths hash to detect and discard duplicates on retry. 4) To support typed unions/variants, include a small strategy registry that maps discriminator fields to constructors. 5) Avoid introducing new C deps; implement in pure Python with optional C-extension fast-path later.
implementation_plan: Spike: implement incremental event parser wrapper around existing streaming JSON tokenizer (2d)
Prototype StreamHydrator core applying path/value events to a mutable state (3d)
Adapter layer: pydantic adapter + dataclass adapter with strict validation toggle (2d)
Checkpoint token format RFC and unit tests for idempotent resume (1d)
Examples and docs: streaming_hydration_demo.py + README section (1d)
API review + iterate on ergonomics with SDK maintainers (half-day)
Merge and small follow-up PERF ticket to profile memory and CPU on large nested streams
test_plan: Unit tests: incremental field patches applied in various orders produce identical final model
Property tests for checkpoint/resume: generate randomized event streams, checkpoint mid-stream, resume and assert equality
Integration: run example against staging streaming endpoint with artificially chunked responses
Fuzz: send truncated/corrupted chunks and assert graceful errors and retry hooks fire
Performance: measure memory consumption vs naive full-buffer approach for 1MB, 10MB, 50MB payloads
comments: 2026-03-02 - Avery Chen: Kickoff spike done. Incremental tokenizer wrapper prototype works with generator of events (path/value). Observed extra overhead from path string allocation; added a TODO to intern common paths.
2026-03-04 - Ravi Kapoor: Reviewed prototype. Suggested adding a strict mode for Pydantic validation and a permissive mode that maps missing fields to defaults to match current SDK behavior.

2026-03-06 - PM feedback (Lina Morales): Make checkpoint token format explicit in docs; customers will want visibility into resume semantics. Also requested an example where SDK resumes an upload-like flow without producing duplicated application-side side-effects.
2026-03-08 - Design review: Kept API surface small (StreamHydrator.apply_event(evt) + StreamHydrator.checkpoint() + StreamHydrator.finalize()). Agreed to keep adapters pluggable for unions.

2026-03-09 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented dataclass adapter and added initial unit tests for merged nested lists. Found an edge-case with list-insert semantics when indices arrive out-of-order; added deterministic buffering of list-tombstones to the plan.
risk: Medium: incorrect merging semantics could lead to subtle data corruption for nested structures. Performance overhead from path/event allocation could degrade throughput. Mitigations: thorough unit/property tests, benchmark against baseline, and an optional C-backed intern pool if allocation cost dominates.
next_steps: Finish PR #1976 prototype and add test coverage for out-of-order list events
Write example that demonstrates idempotent resume for an app that writes to a downstream DB (simulate side-effect dedup keys)
Schedule API review with SDK maintainers and Docs to finalize public helper names
Create follow-up perf ticket after merge to evaluate native accelerations
